rows.claim: A mutable type anywhere in a port value is refused (also D-237's position).
rows.evidence: probe: B.mutable_nested builds with no diagnostic (struct HoldsMut; m::MutS end, MutS mutable, as a port type). src/leaves.jl:99-110 and src/leaves.jl:18 show the walk stops at any concrete immutable non-isbits type as an opaque leaf and never looks inside. probe: B.mutable_port (Vector{Float64} as the port type itself) is refused as IllegalPortType/:mutable. Spec line 1093 itself says the build does not look inside a field handle.
rows.fix: A mutable type the leaf walk reaches is refused, so a port type that is itself mutable, or a static array of one; a mutable reference held inside an opaque leaf is stored whole and is not looked at.
rows.note: Same sentence is in D-237's Position. The code is consistent with the opaque-leaf rule at lines 997-1000 and 1090-1094, so the over-broad word is 'anywhere'. A verifier may rule defect if the intent is to refuse mutable fields inside handles; D-237 'Rejected' (walking into references) argues against that.

rows.claim: Every primitive provides exactly two output stages, y_state and y_direct (also line 889 'the two output stages every primitive provides' and line 1118 'two output stages per primitive').
rows.evidence: probe: C.Negator y_direct and test/fixtures.jl:67-70 (Negator has y_direct only), test/fixtures.jl:49-54 (BareTicker has y_state only); src/declare.jl:768 has_stage asks by method presence; src/build.jl:66 and :1184 skip an absent stage; the spec's own lines 1226-1227 and 1258-1259 admit a component with no stage-1 ports and a stage that may not exist.
rows.fix: Every primitive has two output stage slots, `y_state` (stage 1) and `y_direct` (stage 2), and provides whichever it needs; at least one port is produced by each stage that exists.
rows.note: Wording problem, not a code fault. D-006's own text says only 'strict two-stage structural feedthrough'.

rows.claim: Each field-emitting component also exposes a value-level constructor, a plain public function from its input values to its handle.
rows.evidence: No field-emitting environment component exists in src/. src/library.jl has no handle emitter (rg Field/handle hits only Fields{V}, a struct splitter). The environment components live in the external FlightPhysics package, which is not in W.
rows.note: A convention on library authors (D-139), not enforced by any code in this repo. Nothing to check against.
